correctness.rationale: The method is reconstructed from both component evaluations of the original same-sample SEG stage, yielding \(Mz+\epsilon d\). Every rotation plane satisfies \(M_j^{\mathsf T}M_j=r_j^2I\) and \((M_j-I)^{\mathsf T}(M_j-I)=h_jI\). Independent centered signs remove cross terms exactly, giving the iid and reshuffling geometric-series formulas. Their difference is controlled by \(q_j-1=2(\kappa t_j^2-1)/(1+r_j^2)\), giving necessary and sufficient modal conditions. An active mode above the threshold furnishes strict reverse inequality at every epoch; the remaining modes prove the converse. Contractivity yields unique invariant distributions and the stationary limits. The source-recommended \(\kappa=4\) rational witness has exact \(V_{\mathrm{iid}}=169/31\) and ratio \(1521/971\). Stage-based exact rational enumeration checked 32 finite-history expectations, including a mixed-frequency four-dimensional model. Only the analytic proof establishes the infinite families.

value.rationale: Random reshuffling is a motivated design decision in stochastic variational-inequality solvers. The result gives a necessary-and-sufficient spectral cutoff for its mean-square benefit in an exact noninterpolating common-skew affine family, a stable counterexample using the literature-recommended step ratio, and finite-epoch as well as stationary costs. Rather than a generic reshuffling counterexample, it completely classifies the strict-contraction parameter interval and explains the transition through the paired noise polynomial.
